story: On Magnolia Loop on this partly cloudy Wednesday, Gary is hunting for the Architectural Review blanks while he finishes wiring his golf cart, and he promises Donna a tomorrow morning tennis match. Donna cheerfully offers to trim her flamingo flock to three, but Hal, wary yet fair, reminds her of the ornament rule and asks her to thin the flock before he has to write a violation notice. Meanwhile, in her kitchen, Rosa is optimistically finalizing a grocery list for four and deciding which day to go shopping.
events: Rosa (rosa kitchen): Finalize the grocery list with quantities for four and pick which day to shop

gary.thought_process: I checked the bulletin board last tick looking for the Architectural Review form and came up short. Donna and Hal just wandered up, and Donna already offered to book a court tomorrow so I can finish the cart today. I shouldn't re-invite or re-ask; I should answer her offer and tie it to my promise to get the L-01 form filed before Saturday. Hal's an old hand around here and probably knows where the form actually gets filed. Keep it short and friendly, then get back to the cart.

parameters.content: Tomorrow morning works, Donna, put me down for the court and I'll bring my worst backhand. Today I've got to finish the cart wiring and get that Architectural Review form filed. Either of you know where they keep the blanks?

donna.thought_process: Gary and Hal are both right here on Magnolia Loop. I already have Saturday at 8 AM with Gary penciled in and the spare paddle set aside, so I don't need to re-ask him. Hal is the one I've got a loose end with: those flamingos, and his ornament rule. L-02 caps us at three visible from the street, so I'd rather settle it with a friendly word than get a violation notice. Hal just arrived, so a light, neighborly opener is natural and moves things forward without repeating anything I've already said.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal! I know you've got your eye on my flamingos, so I'll save you the trouble. I'll do a quick count and trim the flock down to three so we're square with the ornament rule. No violation notice needed.

hal.thought_process: I counted flamingos and carts earlier and the notebook says it's a real count, but I've been wondering if I'm keeping the peace or just keeping score. Donna and Gary are both standing here in plain sight, so I can address the flamingos directly instead of filing a complaint behind her back. Ornaments visible from the street are capped at three under L-02. A word to her face is the fair way to handle it before any paperwork goes to the committee.

parameters.content: Donna, I counted your flamingos from the street this morning. L-02 says three ornaments, and you're well past that. Thin the flock before I have to write it up, and I'd rather not.

rosa.thought_process: I've already blocked out Saturday, planned the menu, and locked in the seating for four. Hal and Donna have said yes, and Gary got my invitation through the group chatter but I haven't heard from him directly. Nobody is nearby to talk to, so the useful thing is the grocery list. Pulling up the shift schedule again would just repeat what I did. I'll finalize the shopping list in the kitchen with quantities for four, so I can shop around my shifts.

parameters.content: Finalize the grocery list with quantities for four and pick which day to shop

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
